<section class="article-section">
  <div class="container">

        <h2>The Drifter Manifesto</h2>
        <p style="margin-bottom: 1rem; font-size: 1.1rem; line-height: 1.8; color: var(--text-dark);">
          The Drifter Manifesto is the orientation series for AffineDrift's control-affine
          treatment of biomechanical motion. Read it as a research program with explicit
          provenance: established nonlinear-control mathematics first, then AffineDrift's
          proposed counterfactual diagnostics, then golf-specific modeling hypotheses that
          still require parameter identification and experimental replication.
        </p>
        <div style="margin-bottom: 1.5rem; padding: 0.75rem 1rem; background: var(--bg-secondary, #f8f9fa); border-left: 3px solid var(--primary-color, #2563eb); border-radius: 4px; font-size: 0.9rem; color: var(--text-light, #6b7280);">
          <strong>Provenance:</strong> The smooth control-affine form \(\dot{x}=f(x)+G(x)u\) and drift vector fields are established nonlinear-control tools (Isidori 1995; Bullo and Lewis 2004). ZTCF, ZVCF, and the weighted drift-to-control ratio \(\mathrm{DCR}_{W}\) are AffineDrift diagnostics layered on that foundation. Treat golf-specific ratios and phase labels as model-dependent claims, not peer-reviewed invariants. See <a href="../critiques/index.html">Critiques &amp; Responses</a> for documented limitations.
        </div>
        <div style="margin-bottom: 1.5rem; padding: 0.75rem 1rem; background: var(--bg-secondary, #f8f9fa); border-left: 3px solid var(--primary-color, #2563eb); border-radius: 4px; font-size: 0.9rem; color: var(--text-light, #6b7280);">
          <strong>Notation baseline:</strong> The series uses \(x=(q,\dot{q})\), \(f(x)\) for unforced smooth dynamics, \(G(x)u\) for actuated generalized forces, and \(\mathrm{DCR}_{W}\) only after stating the norm, weighting matrix, torque bound, and model parameters. Counterfactual simulations are valid only within the assumptions stated in each article. Impacts, switching contact, and tissue deformation require separate hybrid or compliant models.
        </div>
        <div style="margin-bottom: 1.5rem; padding: 0.75rem 1rem; background: var(--bg-secondary, #f8f9fa); border-left: 3px solid var(--primary-color, #2563eb); border-radius: 4px; font-size: 0.9rem; color: var(--text-light, #6b7280);">
          <strong>Evidence standard:</strong> Treat each ratio, phase label, and counterfactual conclusion as a modeling claim until the source gives the model, parameter values, sensitivity check, and data source. The manifesto states the research program; it does not by itself establish a clinical, coaching, or universal biomechanical rule.
        </div>
        <div style="margin-bottom: 1.5rem; padding: 0.75rem 1rem; background: var(--bg-secondary, #f8f9fa); border-left: 3px solid var(--primary-color, #2563eb); border-radius: 4px; font-size: 0.9rem; color: var(--text-light, #6b7280);">
          <strong>Publication use:</strong> Use the manifesto as an editorial map, not as a substitute for the technical sources. A claim is ready for stronger public wording only when the corresponding article identifies the coordinate convention, actuator model, contact assumptions, validation data, uncertainty or sensitivity analysis, and whether the key quantity was directly measured or inferred from a model.
        </div>
        <div style="margin-bottom: 1.5rem; padding: 0.75rem 1rem; background: var(--bg-secondary, #f8f9fa); border-left: 3px solid var(--primary-color, #2563eb); border-radius: 4px; font-size: 0.9rem; color: var(--text-light, #6b7280);">
          <strong>Citation practice:</strong> Cite the manifesto for editorial orientation only. Scientific claims repeated from it should also cite the underlying AffineDrift article or external source that carries the derivation, data, or experiment, and should state whether the claim is analytical, simulated, or experimentally supported.
        </div>
        <div style="margin-bottom: 1.5rem; padding: 0.75rem 1rem; background: var(--bg-secondary, #f8f9fa); border-left: 3px solid var(--primary-color, #2563eb); border-radius: 4px; font-size: 0.9rem; color: var(--text-light, #6b7280);">
          <strong>Source map:</strong> For affine notation and drift/input separation, start with <a href="../articles/theory-part1.html">Theory Part 1</a> and <a href="../articles/theory-part2.html">Theory Part 2</a>. For DCR interpretation, compare the <a href="../articles/controllability-drift-ratio.html">DCR article</a> with the <a href="../critiques/index.html">critique index</a>. For inverse-dynamics and observability limits, read <a href="../articles/inverse-dynamics.html">Inverse Dynamics</a>, <a href="../articles/zero-torque-counterfactual.html">Zero Torque Counterfactual</a>, and <a href="../critiques/ztcf_identifiability.html">ZTCF Identifiability</a> before treating a manifesto claim as evidence.
        </div>
        <div style="margin-bottom: 1.5rem; padding: 0.75rem 1rem; background: var(--bg-secondary, #f8f9fa); border-left: 3px solid var(--primary-color, #2563eb); border-radius: 4px; font-size: 0.9rem; color: var(--text-light, #6b7280);">

                <td style="padding: 0.35rem; vertical-align: top;">State the coordinates, actuator convention, and whether contact or impact terms have been excluded.</td>

                <td style="padding: 0.35rem; vertical-align: top;">Separate forward simulation results from measured muscle recruitment, coaching interpretation, and clinical claims.</td>

                <td style="padding: 0.35rem; vertical-align: top;">Separate passive tissue response, reflex or local feedback, measured external forces, and coaching interpretation before claiming that a swing is self-organizing or GRF-driven.</td>

          <h3><a href="../articles/theory-part1.html">Theory Part 1 &mdash; State definition and affine derivation</a></h3>
          <p>Establishes the multibody coordinates, derives the control-affine structure, and sets the notation used in every subsequent article.</p>

          <p>Formalizes how to separate passive dynamics from deliberate torque using zero torque and zero velocity counterfactuals.</p>
